cohorts.subjects: Adults of known sex and age from Sonepat district, Haryana, India (called haryanvis subjects in the abstract), whose plain AP lumbar radiographs came from the Radiology Department of B.P.S.G.M.C. for women, Khanpur Kalan, Sonepat. Inclusion: films diagnosed as normal by experienced radiologists. Exclusion: films with any obvious abnormality. Why they were imaged, dates and whether consecutive are not stated. Inference: living hospital subjects.
cohorts.n_units: 300 AP lumbar radiographs (150 male, 150 female), L1 to L5 measured; per-level n not printed (Inference: 1,500 vertebrae if every level was read on every film)

techniques.instrument: a scale calibrated to 0.5 mm, applied to plain antero-posterior lumbar radiographs
techniques.how: For each lumbar vertebra L1 to L5, the interpedicular distance: the minimum distance between the shadows of the two pedicles of the same vertebra on the AP film, taken as the transverse diameter of the spinal canal. Reported as mean, SD and a calculated range of mean +/- 3 SD by sex and level, with a male-female p-value per level (test not named).
techniques.magnification: not stated and not corrected; tube-film distance and patient position not stated, so values are film millimetres
techniques.observers: not stated in this paper; no repeat readings or reliability figures reported

techniques.modality: dry bone caliper (Eisenstein's own Methods, his p. 173; this paper calls the study radiographic)
techniques.instrument: not stated in this paper; vernier caliper in Eisenstein's own Methods (his p. 173)
techniques.how: quoted in Table II as the mean transverse diameter of the lumbar canal; this paper names Eisenstein 1977 among workers who used plain radiography (p. 34) and gives no definition. Checked against Eisenstein's own pages: the values are his Table I Canal I.P. rows (his p. 174), the greatest interpedicular distance measured with a vernier caliper on dry vertebrae (his p. 173), true size in whole millimetres; his radiographs served only to derive magnification factors (AP 1.14 at 110 cm, his p. 175). Keyed canal_w, as the eisenstein1977 reading keys the same values

quoted in Table II as the mean transverse diameter of the lumbar canal; this paper says the study used the radiographic method (p. 34) and equates the transverse diameter with the IPD; projection, landmarks and definition not given. Inference: a transverse canal width on a radiograph is read on an AP view. Inference (amonookuofi1982 reading): vernier calipers on AP films at 100 cm, shortest distance between the medial pedicle surfaces, no magnification correction

within_paper: One set of subjects: every value of this paper's own comes from the same 300 AP radiographs (p. 34, PDF 2); the 'Present study (sonepat District)' rows of Table II repeat the Table I means (p. 35, PDF 3), and the Abstract and Conclusion counts restate the Methods sample (p. 33, PDF 1; p. 35, PDF 3). The five quoted series of Table II are other studies' subjects, distinct from this paper's; the paper states no overlap among them. The two Eisenstein rows are two groups of one study.
